title: Decomposition of Bernoulli restriction probability by free-variable count
statement:
Fix $n$ and a real parameter $p$ with $0 \le p \le 1$, and let $\mathrm{event}$ be any (decidable) property of restrictions on $n$ variables. Then the probability that $\mathrm{event}$ holds under a Bernoulli($p$) random restriction equals its average over the fixed-size restriction models, weighted by the binomial distribution on the number of free variables:
\[
  \Pr_{p}[\mathrm{event}] \;=\; \sum_{k=0}^{n} \binom{n}{k}\, p^{k}\, (1-p)^{\,n-k}\; R_k(\mathrm{event}),
\]
where $R_k(\mathrm{event})$ is the fraction of restrictions with exactly $k$ free variables that satisfy $\mathrm{event}$.
hypotheses_covered: event is a decidable predicate on restrictions of n variables
replaced:
For $0 \le p \le 1$ and any event, the Bernoulli$(p)$ restriction probability decomposes
according to the number of free variables:
\[
  \Pr_{R_p}[\mathrm{event}] = \sum_{k=0}^{n} \mathrm{binomialPMF}\,n\,p\,k \cdot \mathrm{fixedSizeRestrProb}\,(\mathrm{event})\,k,
\]
because conditioning $R_p$ on having exactly $k$ free variables yields exactly the model $R_k$.
